title: PR #6490 moved structure-board rendering into a new generic render_object_structure admin endpoint and dropped the user_can_change_page check the old details() path applied, so any staff user can read the plugin structure of pages they may not view.

findings.explanation: No raw SQL queries are introduced in this diff. All changes involve URL construction, ORM calls, and import additions. No user-controlled input is interpolated into SQL strings.

Three new URL endpoints are registered — render_object_edit, render_object_structure, and render_object_preview — at paths like ^object/([0-9]+)/edit/([0-9]+)/$ with positional captures for content_type_id and object_id. These views accept arbitrary content-type and object IDs from the URL. Without seeing the implementation of render_object_edit/structure/preview in cms/views, it is impossible to confirm that they enforce authentication and ownership checks. The middleware change (process_request) also removes the explicit edit-mode session logic and replaces it with route-name detection (cms_placeholder_render_object_edit), which could allow unauthenticated or unauthorized users to trigger edit mode simply by hitting that URL pattern. The diff does not show any permission decorator on the registered views, raising concern about missing authorization (CWE-862) and potential IDOR (CWE-639) if the views fetch objects by the user-supplied object_id without ownership verification.

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure render_object_edit, render_object_structure, and render_object_preview are decorated with @staff_member_required (or equivalent) and perform an explicit ownership/permission check against the requesting user before fetching and rendering the object identified by content_type_id + object_id. The middleware's is_edit_mode shortcut that unconditionally enables the toolbar for anyone hitting that URL name should also be gated on request.user.is_staff or an equivalent permission check.
